title: Saaremaa & Muhu: Juniper Island Loop

bestPeriod.window: Late May to mid-September; June for wildflower meadows and midnight-ish light, September for empty roads and warm sea

summary: A seven-day cycling trip itinerary in West Estonian Archipelago, Estonia.

itinerary.title: Virtsu, ferry to Muhu, Koguva village
itinerary.morning: Bus or transfer from Tallinn to Virtsu (about 2 h). Take the TS Laevad ferry Virtsu–Kuivastu, 27 minutes; bikes board with foot passengers.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride west across Muhu to Koguva, an entirely preserved fieldstone-walled fishing village that is now an open-air museum with people still living in it. Stone walls, thatched roofs, juniper everywhere.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Pädaste Manor's Alexander restaurant if you are doing the one splurge night, or the simpler Sea House terrace on the same estate. Sunset over the Muhu strait.

itinerary.title: Muhu to Kuressaare via the Väinatamm causeway
itinerary.morning: East to Liiva and the church with its 13th-century paintings, then across the Väinatamm — a 3.5 km stone causeway built in the 1890s linking Muhu to Saaremaa, dead flat and fully exposed to crosswind.
itinerary.afternoon: Through Orissaare and south on the main road, then peel off onto the coastal gravel via Kõiguste bay. Stop at the Kaali meteorite crater — a 110 m water-filled impact crater about 3,500 years old, small and strange, with eight satellite craters in the woods around it.
itinerary.evening: Arrive Kuressaare. Beer in the town square, dinner at Ku-Kuu in the old town.

itinerary.title: Kuressaare, castle day and a short spin
itinerary.morning: Kuressaare Episcopal Castle — the best-preserved medieval fortress in the Baltics, a square limestone keep with a full moat and bastions. Give it three hours; the Saaremaa Museum inside is thorough.
itinerary.afternoon: Easy flat ride west to Nasva harbour and the Sõrve road's first stretch. Swim at Mändjala's shallow pine-backed beach.
itinerary.evening: Saaremaa's spa culture is real and cheap. Book an evening slot at one of the Kuressaare spa hotels — sauna, seawater pools, and a mud treatment for the price of a city cocktail.

itinerary.title: Sõrve peninsula out-and-back
itinerary.morning: South down the Sõrve peninsula, a 32 km finger of land pointing at Latvia. Ride the west-coast road via Järve and Lõu; almost no traffic.
itinerary.afternoon: Sõrve lighthouse at the tip, 52 m, climbable, with the Gulf of Riga on one side and the open Baltic on the other. The peninsula was the site of brutal 1944 fighting — bunkers and the Sõrve Military Museum are along the return.
itinerary.evening: Return north to Kuressaare on the east-coast road for variety. Long day; eat early and well.

itinerary.title: Northwest coast: Panga cliff and Mustjala
itinerary.morning: North through Kihelkonna's flatlands, onto compacted limestone gravel through juniper heath — this is the classic Saaremaa surface and it rides beautifully on 35 mm tyres.
itinerary.afternoon: Panga cliff (Panga pank), a 21 m limestone escarpment straight down into the sea, the highest on the island and an old sacrificial site. Continue to Mustjala.
itinerary.evening: Stay in a Mustjala-area farm guesthouse. Smoked fish, home-brewed island beer, and dark skies.

itinerary.title: Vilsandi National Park and Angla
itinerary.morning: West to Loona and the Vilsandi National Park visitor centre. At low water and with a guide, the Vilsandi crossing to the island is a wading and shallow-boat affair; otherwise ride the Harilaid peninsula to Kiipsaare lighthouse, which leans in the sea like a small Baltic Pisa.
itinerary.afternoon: East to Angla windmill hill — five wooden windmills on a ridge, the classic Saaremaa image — and the Karja church nearby with its unusual carved stone reliefs.
itinerary.evening: Back to Kuressaare or Orissaare depending on your ferry time tomorrow.

itinerary.title: Muhu, ferry, and out
itinerary.morning: Cross the causeway back to Muhu, ride the northern lane past Muhu ostrich farm and the Muhu bread bakery, and reach Kuivastu with an hour spare.
itinerary.afternoon: Ferry to Virtsu, bus to Tallinn (about 2 h), leaving a Tallinn evening if you want it.

accommodationStrategy.name: Pädaste Manor
accommodationStrategy.description: Restored 16th-century estate on the south Muhu shore, spa in the old stables, Alexander restaurant working almost exclusively from island produce. Perfect first or last night: it is 20 minutes from the ferry, so it absorbs travel-day fatigue, and it has covered bike storage.

accommodationStrategy.name: Grand Rose SPA Hotel / Georg Ots Spa Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: Two mid-price spa hotels a few minutes from the castle. The point is the recovery: thermal pools, saunas and a masseur on the premises after the Sõrve day. Both accept bikes in luggage rooms — ask when booking rather than on arrival.

accommodationStrategy.name: Farm guesthouses around Mustjala and Kihelkonna
accommodationStrategy.description: Family-run, €50–70 a double, breakfast included and dinner if you ask by lunchtime. This is where the trip stops being a route and starts being Saaremaa. Book direct by phone or email; many are not on international platforms.

logistics.connectivity: Estonia has excellent, cheap mobile data island-wide including the Sõrve tip. E-services (ferry tickets, bus tickets, parking) are all app-based and work in English.
logistics.emergency: 112. Kuressaare Hospital is the only full facility; the Sõrve peninsula and northwest gravel are 45–60 minutes from it.
logistics.weather: Continental-maritime: warm calm Junes, but gales are possible any month and the causeway is fully exposed. Sea temperature peaks at 18–20 °C in early August.
logistics.bookingWindows: Pädaste Manor: 3+ months for summer weekends. Kuressaare spa hotels: 4–6 weeks. Bike rental: reserve 2–3 weeks out and confirm the rack and pannier situation in writing.

other.label: Ferries
other.text: TS Laevad runs Virtsu–Kuivastu roughly hourly in season. Foot passengers with bikes almost never need a reservation; cars very much do in July. Timetables shift seasonally. `verify: true`

other.label: Ticks
other.text: Saaremaa is a genuine tick-borne encephalitis area. TBE vaccination is recommended for anyone riding gravel and stopping in meadows and long grass. Check daily; use permethrin-treated socks.

other.label: Roads
other.text: Estonian drivers are courteous but rural speed limits are 90 km/h. Daytime running lights are mandatory for cars, and reflective elements are legally required for pedestrians and strongly advised for cyclists after dusk.

proTips: Come in **early June**: the alvar meadows — thin-soil limestone grassland with wild orchids — are at their peak, and Saaremaa has some of Europe's richest orchid populations.
Saaremaa's home-brewed farmhouse beer (*koduõlu*) is a living tradition, not a revival. Ask a guesthouse host; it is rarely sold commercially and almost never exported.
Book the **spa evening**, not the spa morning. Estonian spa hotels are half-empty after 20:00 and the day-guest crowd is gone.
The Kaali crater car park is jammed 11:00–14:00 with coach tours off the Muhu ferry. Ride there at **16:30** instead.
Carry cash of €20–40. Village shops and farm stalls in the west take cards, but a few honesty boxes and the smallest smokehouses do not.
If the wind turns hard westerly, flip Days 4 and 5 — Sõrve into a 12 m/s headwind for 32 km is the one way to make this easy island hard.
